# SB-1005 — Safety bulletin: pinch points during die change

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-CN02

Hazard description

Pinch point incidents have been observed during die change activities where personnel enter the immediate die area while lowering, aligning, or securing dies. The primary hazards are entrapment between die halves, accidental actuation of clamping or ejection systems, and unexpected movement of handling fixtures. Secondary hazards include contact with rotating components during setup and interaction with maintenance tooling in confined spaces. Contributing factors identified in recent reviews include incomplete lockout/tagout, inadequate communication between press operator and rigging personnel, and lack of dedicated exclusion zones during lift and alignment operations.

Background and rationale

Die change is an inherently high-risk activity at the interface between heavy tooling and powered machinery. The process mixes powered motion, suspended loads, and manual alignment tasks in a space where body parts can be unawarely positioned in danger zones. Preventing pinch injuries requires layered controls: administrative controls to govern who may perform tasks, engineering controls to restrict movement and isolate hazards, and procedural controls to ensure safe work sequencing.

The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 70 hours. This equipment-specific maintenance note is cited to emphasize that lubrication and machine condition are part of a broader machine safeguarding program; poorly maintained components can produce unexpected motion during setup and increase the likelihood of pinch exposures.

Affected equipment

This bulletin applies to the equipment and work areas used during die change activities on the production die press and associated handling aids on line P3-L3, specifically including EQ-P3-L3-CN02 when used for die modification, trimming, or probe verification prior to press installation. The controls described must be applied where dies are stored, lifted, and placed, and where supplemental machining or inspection of die faces occurs.

Required controls

Engineering and physical controls
- Create and maintain physically defined exclusion zones around the die footprint during change operations. Barriers must prevent entry into the immediate die area while lifting and aligning operations are in progress.
- Use mechanical stops or temporary shimming devices that physically prevent die halves from closing or shifting when personnel are in the work envelope.
- Ensure all lifting fixtures and hoists are rated and inspected per existing maintenance programs before use. If EQ-P3-L3-CN02 is used for die-related machining of components, verify lubrication status per machine maintenance records prior to die movement; refer to maintenance documentation in MM-P3-L3-CN02.
- Where possible, install or deploy mechanical interlocks that prevent activation of clamping systems while personnel are inside the exclusion zone.

Administrative controls and procedure adherence
- All die change tasks must follow the written sequence in SOP-P3-L3-01 and SOP-P3-L3-02. These procedures define responsibility, communication protocol, and sequence of machine and rigging actions. No deviation is permitted without prior authorization and documented risk assessment.
- Require a pre-task brief that identifies roles, confirms completion of lockout/tagout, and reviews the exclusion zone boundary. Verbal confirmation of hazard awareness must be recorded in the job sign-off log.
- Lockout/tagout must be applied to all energy sources that could cause die motion, including hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, and electrical systems. Verify isolation using the multi-point verification method described in SOP-P3-L3-02 before any personnel enter the die envelope.

Work sequencing and communication
- Establish a single point of authority responsible for final go/no-go clearance during lift and alignment. That person must be recognized by all crew members and their authority recorded in the job log.
- Use a standardized communications method for all hand signals and radio calls used during die handling. Confirm receipt of each control command and maintain a continuous acknowledgment until completion of the sequence.

Personal protective equipment and human factors
- Mandate PPE that provides clear visibility and does not interfere with ability to receive visual or audio signals. Prohibit loose clothing or accessories that could snag during handling.
- Limit personnel in the exclusion zone to those necessary to perform alignment tasks. Ensure that all assigned personnel have been trained in the relevant SOPs and can demonstrate task competency.

Examples and scenario guidance

Example scenario: During a lift, a die half shifts and a technician reaches between the die faces to reposition a locator. With no temporary stop in place and incomplete lockout, the die shifted and created a pinch exposure. Preventive steps demonstrated here include confirming mechanical stops are installed, confirming lockout is complete, and maintaining the exclusion zone until the stop is verified.

Example scenario: EQ-P3-L3-CN02 was used to machine a die component and was returned to the press area without confirmation of machine maintenance. A lubrication issue caused unexpected chatter during a trial fit, leading to a surprise movement when clamp engagement was attempted. To prevent recurrence, follow MM-P3-L3-CN02 before and after using machining equipment, and log lubrication status as part of pre-install checklists.

Records to keep

Maintain task-specific records in the die change job folder. Required records include:
- Pre-task brief sign-off and role assignments.
- Lockout/tagout verification documentation for isolation of all energy sources.
- Inspection and test records for lifting gear and temporary stops, retained with the job folder.
- Reference to machine maintenance status for EQ-P3-L3-CN02 as documented in MM-P3-L3-CN02 when that machine is involved in die preparation.
- Procedure adherence verification using SOP-P3-L3-01 and SOP-P3-L3-02 checklists showing completion of required steps.

Audit and enforcement

Supervisors must review job folders after each die change and confirm that records are complete and any deviations were authorized and documented. Noncompliance with required controls shall be addressed through immediate corrective actions and retraining per plant compliance protocols.

Effective date

Effective date: See Document Control for release timestamp.

Related documents

MM-P3-L3-CN02  
SOP-P3-L3-01  
SOP-P3-L3-02

Distribution and questions

This bulletin must be distributed to all personnel assigned to die change activities on line P3-L3 and to maintenance staff responsible for EQ-P3-L3-CN02. Direct questions or requests for clarification to the Safety Coordinator through the standard document control channel.
